_readme: THE SERVED-CHANNEL REGISTER — [pipeline R-5] company/pipeline/09-release-engineering.md
The complete set of channels this factory can release to: what artifact each one accepts, what
signing identity it needs, which lane produces it, which toolchain floor gates it, and — the field
everything else hangs off — whether it is SERVED today.
WHY IT EXISTS. Nine acceptance criteria across stages 9 and 10 quantify over 'the served set', and
until this file landed that set did not exist. An undefined right-hand side cannot reject anything,
so all nine reported clean over nothing:
[9]R-3  every signing identity is enumerated and applied    -> signing.* on every row
[9]R-4  a release artifact outlives the run that made it    -> artifactFormats + served flag
[9]R-5  release only to declared channels, never a partial  -> this file + aggregatingJob
[9]R-6  every artifact names the gated commit it came from  -> lane.*
[10]D-1 no channel is claimed that is not served            -> platforms x served
[10]D-4 every store channel has a publisher account         -> kind=store + ownerQueue
[10]D-5 store listing metadata generated from the spec      -> storeMetadataDir +
storeMetadataContract
[10]D-9 what is live on which channel, machine-answerable   -> deploymentEnvironment
[10]D-10 each store channel has a repeatable submission path -> submittable + submission
TWO OTHER GUARDS READ THIS FILE and are not listed above because they are not R-5's:
tooling/ci/assert-store-metadata.mjs        [10]D-5  — the expected metadata-tree set is
{ kind:"store" rows } x { apps }, the per-tree file list is `storeMetadataContract`, and
the MSIX identity a row declares is compared to what apps/*/pubspec.yaml packages with.
tooling/release/submit-windows-store.mjs    [10]D-10 — the same contract, read by the release
tooling/release/submit-play.mjs             [10]D-10 — path rather than by CI. They re-check
independently on purpose: a release path that trusts a check it did not run is not a release
path. Each reads only ITS OWN row, so neither can be made to pass by the other's channel.
🔴 THE ONE RULE THAT MAKES THIS FILE MEAN ANYTHING: `served` IS THE GATE, NOT MEMBERSHIP.
A row here is NOT a claim that the factory ships to that channel. Rows exist for channels that are
deferred, so their researched facts (formats, identities, toolchain floors, real costs) are recorded
once instead of rediscovered at submission time. Only `served: true` licenses a claim in
sites/_shared/_data/apps.json. Adding "windows" to an app's `platforms` array fails the build today
precisely because both windows rows exist and neither is served.
Enforced by tooling/ci/assert-channel-register.mjs:
· every apps.json `platforms` value resolves to a SERVED row here          [R-5, D-1]
· every SERVED row's platforms are claimed by a real app — a served channel nobody ships to
is the 'six platforms' lie growing back                                  [R-5, cut 5 corollary]
· every SERVED row with a real keyKind carries a NAMED identity and a DATED restore drill
(the row's own `required` flag cannot waive it — hardened 2026-07-31), plus a lane
that resolves to a real workflow JOB, a deployment-environment template, and a pinned
toolchain floor                                                          [R-3, R-4, R-6, D-9]
· `artifactFormats` and `minimumToolchain` are non-empty arrays of non-empty STRINGS, and a row's
formats are COMPARED TO WHAT ITS LANE BUILDS: a served row whose lane emits none of the formats
it accepts FAILS, a deferred row's gap PRINTS every run (added 2026-07-31 — before it, the
'.aab required, `flutter build apk` shipped' contradiction two rows down could never fail a
build)                                                                    [R-3, R-4]
· `keyKinds` below IS the vocabulary rows are validated against — the guard derives it from this
file instead of carrying its own copy, so deleting the dictionary or renaming an entry out from
under the rows still using it fails                                       [F-2]
· a row's `lane`, when it has one, resolves to a real workflow JOB whether the row is served or
not (hardened 2026-08-01): a DEFERRED row's lane is how [10]D-5/D-10 build the path BEFORE the
account exists, and until this check a deferred lane could name a job nobody had written
· every secret a row declares as signing material carries a WRITTEN `why`, exactly as every
`ciSecretRegister.nonSigning` entry does (added 2026-08-08). The partition had that rule on ONE
SIDE ONLY, so for any row section 9 cannot reach — every non-Android row — pasting a name into
`signing.ciSecrets.names` silenced the undeclared-secret failure with no reason recorded and
nothing for a reviewer to disagree with                                    [9]R-3 limb 2
· a `signing.*` block carrying a `notYetConfiguredSentinel` (a pinned certificate fingerprint or
public key) is dated, sourced and either FULLY on its sentinel or FULLY real. A SERVED row still
on the sentinel FAILS, a deferred row PRINTS, and a HALF-configured block fails in either state —
the same rule `packageIdentity` follows, for the same reason: a half-filled identity packages and
ships cleanly under the wrong name                                          [9]R-3
· every `kind: store` row names an `ownerQueue` id. SHAPE ONLY: CI cannot read OWNER_QUEUE.md
(see below), but a store row with no id at all is checkable here          [D-4]
· the aggregating job's `needs` equals every other job in its workflow — the 'never a partial
set' half, which is how a new platform job silently stops being required  [R-5]
· disqualified channels are named with the LOCKED ADR that killed them, and printed every run
· COVERAGE LOST when the register is absent, empty, or has nothing served   [D-1 requires loud]
⚠️ `ownerQueue` IDS ARE DATA, NOT AN ASSERTION. company/ is gitignored (.gitignore:15) and is not
in the public repo, so no CI guard can read OWNER_QUEUE.md. [10]D-4's machine limbs as written are
unimplementable in CI for that reason — they are a LOCAL check. Recorded here so the ids are at
least in one place a guard could reach if company/ ever ships.
⚠️ MINIMUM TOOLCHAIN NAMES KEYS, NOT VALUES. [pipeline F-2] says every version is declared once;
duplicating '3.44.8' here would make this file the second declaration and the first to drift. So a
row names the tooling/versions.json KEYS that gate it, and the guard asserts they are pinned there.
A served row naming an unpinned key FAILS; a deferred row naming one PRINTS.
🟢 THE PRINT DID ITS JOB AND IS NOW SILENT. These lines used to end '— which is how Apple's Xcode 26
floor stays visible without blocking CI on an owner-deferred channel', because the two Apple rows
named an `xcode` key versions.json did not have. It has one as of 2026-08-08 (`"xcode": "26"`, with
$xcode_comment recording Apple's dated requirement and $updateExemptions recording why no bot can
advance a store-policy floor), so the gap is closed and the guard prints nothing for it. Corrected
here in the same change: a sentence describing a gap that has closed reads as a live gap forever.

_why: [R-5] 'a release either produces the complete artifact set for its declared channels or produces
nothing.' The aggregating job is that half. It is already built and correct — it fails on any
`failure` or `cancelled` across `needs.*` — but nothing checked that `needs` still LISTS every
job. Add a seventh platform job and forget one line, and the aggregate goes green over a set it
no longer covers, which is this repo's single most repeated failure wearing a YAML hat.
[10]D-5's REQUIRED_COVERAGE, expressed as a RELATIONSHIP rather than a number: every app that
could serve a `kind: store` row carries that row's `storeMetadataDir`, and every such directory
carries every file named here. It grows with the register — add a store channel and the coverage
requirement grows with it — so it cannot be a count somebody lowers.
🔴 IT LIVES HERE AND NOT IN THE GUARD BECAUSE TWO THINGS READ IT: tooling/ci/
assert-store-metadata.mjs and tooling/release/submit-windows-store.mjs. A private copy in either
would be the second declaration and the first to drift — the same reasoning that moved `keyKinds`
out of assert-channel-register.mjs. Emptying `requiredFiles` is COVERAGE LOST, not a pass.
⚠️ THE REPO-NATIVE TREE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH AND FASTLANE TREES ARE GENERATED FROM IT.
fastlane's `deliver` covers ios+mac and `supply` covers android — there is NO fastlane path for
Microsoft Store, Snap/AppImage or Web, and Microsoft is the first channel this factory can
actually register. A fastlane layout as the source of truth could only ever describe half the
portfolio, and the half it could not describe would get hand-typed into a console as the only
copy — the exact outcome [10]D-5 exists to prevent.

derivedFields._why: GENERATED FROM THE SPEC is [10]D-5's headline, and a README saying so is not a mechanism. Each entry names the ONE place the value already lives, and the guard compares the file to it — so a listing edited in a console and pasted back here without touching the spec fails the build instead of quietly forking.
_brickVarWhy: `brickVar` names the mason var the BRICK's template must interpolate for this field, and it is
what lets assert-store-metadata.mjs ask the FACTORY the same question it asks a shipped app.
Both vars are written by hooks/pre_gen.dart into the vars mason hands the templates AND
post_gen.dart, so the catalogue row and the listing title are the same string by construction
rather than by two spellings agreeing today.

_why: 🔴 THESE TWO WERE `appConfig` FIELDS AND THE SCAN DID NOT REACH A STAMPED APP. The lookup was
`apps/{app}/lib/core/config/app_config.dart` — apps/subly's layout. The BRICK stamps
`lib/core/app_config.dart`, so for every app the factory produces the file was simply not
there and the guard PRINTED `CANNOT DERIVE` instead of comparing. A print is the quiet half of
this repository's signature defect: the check reported healthy about a file it never opened.
And `contactUrl` could not be fixed by moving the lookup, because the brick's app_config does
not declare it AT ALL — nor should it. assert-stamp-properties.mjs treats every
`https://nikatru.com/<page>.html` constant in that file as a LEGAL page that check-site-integrity
.mjs must publish in LEGAL_PAGES and the settings screen must link; contact.html is a support
page, not a legal document, and forcing it into that set to satisfy a listing field would drag a
1000-character legal-text floor onto a contact page. Wrong shape.
So the portfolio's two listing URLs are declared HERE, once, and both limbs read them: the
per-app trees and the brick's templates. `appConfigPaths` below still exists and is still
checked — `privacyUrl` must AGREE with every app_config that declares it, in both layouts — so
moving the declaration bought reach without losing the tie to the code.
🔴 EVERY NUMBER IN THIS BLOCK CARRIES ITS CITATION, AND A FIELD WITH NO SOURCED LIMIT
CARRIES NONE. An invented limit fires on CORRECT input — a made-up '120 characters or fewer'
once rejected this repo's own fixture at 129 — so a field whose limit was not fetched from a
primary source is recorded as UNVERIFIED in apps/{app}/store/<channel>/README.md and is NOT
given a number here. The guard refuses to enforce a `max` that arrives without a `source`,
so the only way to add a limit is to add its citation with it.
Two limit kinds, because two different things are being counted:
`maxLines` — countable ENTRIES, one per non-blank line (MS Store search terms).
`maxChars` — CHARACTERS of the trimmed field (Apple's name and subtitle; Play's name,
short description and full description).
⚠️ `maxChars` COUNTS UNICODE CODE POINTS of the trimmed file, not UTF-16 units and not bytes.
Neither Apple nor Google publishes the counting RULE — Google says only that 'Character limits
apply to both full-width and half-width characters' — so code points are the closest defensible
reading: a byte count would reject correct UTF-8 prose, and a UTF-16 length would score one
astral character as two and reject copy the store accepts. A correct limit counted the wrong way
fires on correct input exactly like an invented one. Whether a newline inside a description
counts is UNVERIFIED, so newlines ARE counted — the strict direction, which can only reject copy
already sitting on a limit we did not set.

search-terms.txt.source: Microsoft Store Policies v7.19 §10.1.3, verbatim: "Not exceed seven unique terms or phrases."

_why: Apple's listing has fields no other store has, so they are additionalFiles rather than
contract-wide ones: `subtitle.txt` (a real App Store field, 30 chars), `keywords.txt` and
`promotional-text.txt`. The last two are carried because the FIELDS exist and the listing
would otherwise be hand-typed into App Store Connect as the only copy — their LIMITS are a
different question and are UNVERIFIED, see below.
⚠️ `short-description.txt` is NOT Apple's subtitle. The contract requires it in every tree
and Apple has no field of that name; it is the repo-native line the ≤30 subtitle is
condensed FROM. Mapping the 37-character tagline onto a 30-character field would fail on
correct input, which is the exact failure mode this file exists to avoid.
THE ONLY TWO APPLE NUMBERS THAT WERE SOURCED. company/pipeline/10-distribution-store.md
D-5's limits table records the rest as COULD-NOT-ESTABLISH against the same fetch — the
keywords field, description and promotional text are NOT on the page that carries Name
and Subtitle, and the corpus's '100 chars' for keywords is not on it either. They are
therefore absent here and marked UNVERIFIED in the tree's README, not guessed at.

_why: ⚠️ NO CHARACTER LIMIT IS DECLARED FOR THIS CHANNEL AND THAT IS THE FINDING, NOT AN
OVERSIGHT. No Snap Store listing limit was fetched from a primary source in this increment,
so none is enforced — the same rule that leaves Apple's keywords field unnumbered. They are
recorded as UNVERIFIED in apps/{app}/store/linux-snap/README.md.
`snap-name.txt` is the field with real consequences: it is the GLOBAL Snap Store namespace,
claimed once with `snapcraft register <name>` (OWNER_QUEUE A-6) and never transferable
casually. It is carried in the tree so the name we intend to claim is reviewable and diffable
BEFORE it is claimed, rather than being decided at a terminal prompt.
🔴 `license.txt` IS THE LICENCE THE STORE LISTING SHOWS, AND IT IS NOT NECESSARILY AN SPDX
IDENTIFIER. This line said "`license.txt` is the SPDX identifier the store listing shows", and
the file has said `proprietary` the whole time — which is TRUE about the licence and is not an
SPDX identifier at all. The contradiction sat here unnoticed until the first real pack refused
the recipe built from it: `cannot validate license "proprietary": unknown license: proprietary`
(run 31294305898, 2026-08-09). The wrong half was this sentence, not the file.
Where the two meet is tooling/release/generate-snapcraft.mjs: `NON_SPDX_LICENCES` records the
values that cannot be emitted as snapcraft's `license:` key WITH the reason, and the recipe then
omits the key entirely — which the Snap Store reads as `Proprietary` anyway. So the listing keeps
the true word and the recipe reaches the same answer by the only route snapd accepts. Sources are
on that constant; assert-snapcraft-generable.mjs holds both directions.
Google Play publishes its three listing limits plainly, which is why this row carries numbers
where windows-store carries UNVERIFIED marks. All three are from the SAME page, fetched
2026-07-29 and recorded in [10]D-5's limits table:
support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9859152 — app name 30, short description
80, full description 4000, with the note 'Character limits apply to both full-width and
half-width characters'.
🔴 THE 30-CHARACTER TITLE IS THE ONE THAT ACTUALLY BITES. title.txt is DERIVED from
apps.json `name`, so the day an app is stamped with a name longer than 30 characters this
limit fails the build instead of the Play Console rejecting it after a human has already
filled in a submission form. That is the entire value of putting the number here.
`additionalFiles` carries NO listing-text field: Play has no search-terms box. Keywords on Play
come from the title and descriptions themselves, which is a different mechanism from Microsoft's
explicit term list — recording an empty file for it would invent a field the console does not have.
🔴 WHAT IT DOES CARRY IS THE THREE SWORN DECLARATIONS, AND THEY ARE HERE FOR THE SAME REASON THE
LISTING TEXT IS. `data-safety.json` and `content-rating.json` are the Data safety form and the
IARC content-rating questionnaire — Console artefacts that until 2026-08-04 had NO representation
in this repository at all, which apps/subly/store/android-play/README.md recorded in prose as a
blocking gap. They are not listing copy, so they carry no character limit and no `derivedFields`
entry; they are declarations ABOUT THE CODE, and tooling/ci/assert-play-declarations.mjs is what
compares them to it.
`ads-declaration.json` is the THIRD, added 2026-08-09, and it was missing for a reason worth
recording: both of the others answer their advertising question from PACKAGE TELLS — a pubspec
walk for ad SDKs — while the App content → Ads declaration is decided by FORMAT. Google's own
trigger list includes 'House ads: My app renders a small ad banner, interstitial ad, ad wall,
and/or widget', which needs no SDK, no dependency and no permission. So a house-ad surface could
land while every dependency-keyed answer in this tree stayed GREEN and became FALSE, and the
console answer that puts the 'Contains ads' badge on the listing existed nowhere at all.
tooling/ci/assert-ads-declarations.mjs derives it from the shipped widget tree and the served
config payload, and cross-checks all four advertising claims against that one derivation.
Listing them HERE rather than only inside those guards is the load-bearing part. This block is
what makes assert-store-metadata.mjs and tooling/release/submit-play.mjs require the files to be
present and non-empty; off it, any could be deleted or emptied and only one guard would notice
— one guard too few for a declaration Google explicitly holds the developer to the accuracy of.
assert-play-declarations.mjs and assert-ads-declarations.mjs each assert their own membership of
this list and COVERAGE LOST if it is dropped, so the halves cannot come apart quietly. It is also
what makes assert-sworn-store-files.mjs DERIVE the sworn set: every .json here must have a spec
in that guard, so a fourth declaration cannot ship with no floor at all.
🔴 THE THIRD THING A PLAY LISTING NEEDS, AND THE ONE THAT HAD NO REPO REPRESENTATION AT ALL.
The listing TEXT has had a guard on every field since [10]D-5; the two SWORN DECLARATIONS got
theirs on 2026-08-04. The GRAPHICS had neither an artefact nor a number — apps/subly/store/
android-play/screenshots/README.md carried a table with six rows all marked UNVERIFIED and the
instruction 'do not fill a number in from memory'. This block is that table, fetched.
Every number below is quoted from ONE primary page, read in full on 2026-08-04:
https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9866151
Anything that page does NOT state is in `_unverified` and is NOT enforced — an invented limit
fires on CORRECT input, and this repo has already rejected its own fixture at 129 characters
against a made-up '120 or fewer'. The guard refuses any limit that arrives without a `source`,
exactly like maxChars above, so a number cannot be added here without its citation.
⚠️ `alpha` IS A REQUIREMENT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND THE TWO ASSETS DISAGREE. Google requires a
'24-bit PNG (no alpha)' for the feature graphic and screenshots, and a '32-bit PNG (with alpha)'
for the store icon. One rasteriser flag decides it, so getting it backwards produces a file that
looks perfect locally and is refused at upload. tooling/ci/assert-listing-assets.mjs checks the
PNG colour type of each asset against ITS OWN answer rather than against a single house rule.
🔴 WHY THE TWO GRAPHICS ARE ALSO IN `additionalFiles` ABOVE. That list is what makes
assert-store-metadata.mjs require a file to be present and non-empty. Declaring the graphics
ONLY here would mean one guard covering them; the same reasoning that put data-safety.json in
both places applies, and for the same reason — a listing asset that can be deleted while a
guard still reports the tree complete is a listing asset nobody is really holding.

Highly recommended, verbatim: "For apps, you must provide at least four screenshots with minimum 1080px resolution. These should be 16:9 for landscape (minimum 1920x1080px) screenshots and 9:16 for portrait screenshots (minimum 1080x1920px)."
_provenanceWhy: 🔴 A PNG CARRIES NO EVIDENCE OF WHICH BUILD IT PHOTOGRAPHED, AND THAT IS THE ONE QUESTION
THAT MATTERS ABOUT A LISTING SCREENSHOT. Until #150 every store build of this app was a DEMO
build, and a demo build is a different app on screen: app_shell.dart paints 'Demo data - sample
subscriptions, not your account' across every screen, and demo_data.dart fills the board with
Netflix, Spotify, Disney+, Adobe CC and 1Password. Both were confirmed by capturing the demo
build on 2026-08-04 and looking at the result — the banner and two of the trademarks are in
the first frame.
So a screenshot in this directory must be accompanied by CAPTURE.json recording posture:
'live'. The capture script writes the file only on a live run, and refuses to write demo
output into this directory at all. The record must also AGREE with the directory — its count
and its pixel size are both independently measured, because a record describing a different
set is evidence about screenshots that are not these, which is worse than no record at all.
🔴 AND SINCE 2026-08-04 THE BANNER ITSELF IS MEASURED. These lines used to end 'No guard can
read a banner out of a PNG without a rasteriser and an OCR pass' — true of a guard that reads
PNG HEADERS, which is what assert-listing-assets.mjs was, and it quietly turned a limitation
into a policy. CAPTURE.json is a CLAIM: anybody can write one next to any five PNGs. The
banner needs no OCR because it is not text-shaped to a detector — app_shell.dart paints a
full-width Container of AppColors.warn at top:0, so a row through it is almost entirely one
exact colour edge to edge. The guard decodes each frame and looks for that band, with the
colour read live from the design-system token file rather than pinned, and it self-tests the
detector on every run so the limb cannot go dark while this directory is still empty.

_unverified: MAX FILE SIZE FOR A PHONE SCREENSHOT — the page states a maximum only for the app icon (1024KB)
and for Android XR screenshots ('up to 8 MB each'). It states NONE for phone screenshots, so
none is enforced and none is written down. The widely-repeated '8MB' figure is the XR number
WHETHER PHONE SCREENSHOTS ALONE SATISFY THE MINIMUM. The requirement reads 'a minimum of two
screenshots ACROSS DIFFERENT DEVICE TYPES', which does not say whether two phone screenshots
and no tablet ones clear it. The strict reading is enforced (>= 2 in the phone set), because
the loose one can only accept a listing Play might refuse.
TABLET / CHROMEBOOK / WEAR / TV / AUTOMOTIVE / XR SETS. The page states requirements for each,
but this app declares none of those form factors, so no expectation is recorded for them. Add
the row in the same increment that adds the form factor, with this page re-fetched.

keyKinds.none: the channel signs for us — nothing of ours can be lost
keyKinds.upload-key: we sign the upload; the store holds the real app signing key (Play App Signing)
keyKinds.app-signing-key: we hold the key end users' installs are bound to — loss is unrecoverable
keyKinds.distribution-certificate: an Apple distribution certificate + provisioning profile
keyKinds.code-signing-certificate: a CA-issued certificate chaining to a trusted root — a real recurring cost
keyKinds.own-signing-key: our own detached signature, no gatekeeper verifying it for us

_why: 🔴 [9]R-3 LIMB 2 — 'a guard fails if a release build target's signing configuration ... names a
secret that is not in the declared signing-identity register.' Until 2026-08-06 NOTHING IN THE
REPOSITORY READ `signing.ciSecrets` — `grep -rl ciSecrets` returned this file and nothing else.
The four Play names sat here as documentation while android-signing.mjs parsed its names out of
build.gradle.kts, so the register was not the authority the requirement says it is: a workflow
could name ANY secret and no check anywhere compared it to a declaration.
WHY THIS BLOCK IS NEEDED AT ALL, rather than just reading `signing.ciSecrets`. The failing
condition is 'names a secret that is NOT in the register', and a release workflow legitimately
names ~20 secrets that are not signing identities — API_BASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, a store's
upload credentials. Checking only against the signing names would fail every workflow in the
tree; checking only the four that happen to look Android-ish would be a hardcoded classifier
that silently mis-files the next secret somebody adds. So the register carries BOTH SIDES of a
PARTITION: a secret a workflow names is either signing material on a channel row, or it is
declared here as NOT signing material, with a reason. Anything else FAILS — which means a new
secret cannot enter a lane without a human classifying it, and the fail-closed direction is the
one that matters (an unclassified secret defaults to 'stop', never to 'assume it is harmless').
⚠️ THIS LIST IS NOT A SECURITY BOUNDARY AND MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE. It records what each name
IS, so that a signing identity cannot arrive unenumerated. It says nothing about who may read a
secret at runtime — GitHub's environment protection rules are the only thing that does.
A `why` is REQUIRED on every entry, and the guard enforces it. Without it the cheapest way to
silence a failure is to paste the name into this array, which converts a classification decision
into a copy-paste and re-opens exactly the hole limb 2 closes.
🔴 THAT ARGUMENT IS ABOUT THE PARTITION, AND A PARTITION HAS TWO SIDES — which this block did not
notice until 2026-08-08. The rule lived HERE only, so the cheapest way to silence the same failure
was to paste the name into a row's `signing.ciSecrets.names` instead: unreasoned, unreviewed, and
on the SIGNING side of the partition, which is the more expensive place to be wrong. Section 9
hides that for the Android row by comparing its list to build.gradle.kts name for name; no other
row has a build file to compare against, and the four registered on that date have no lane at all.
So `signing.ciSecrets.why` is now required and enforced identically, with the same 20-character
floor reused rather than re-chosen — two thresholds for one property is [pipeline F-2] in miniature.

kinds.publishing-credential: authenticates an upload or deploy to a distribution channel. It authorises PUBLISHING; it is not key material any artifact is signed with — the channel either re-signs (MS Store, Snap) or holds the signing key itself (Play App Signing).
kinds.service-credential: authenticates CI to a backend service it operates on (Supabase management, service-role access). Never enters an artifact and signs nothing.
kinds.build-config: a value compiled into or read by a build — an endpoint, a project ref, a publishable key. Held as a repository secret to keep it out of the public tree, not because it is signing material.

signing.custody: recorded in the private SSoT (OWNER_QUEUE S-4 / reconciliation #25). Redacted here 2026-07-31: a public register must say THAT custody is recorded, never WHERE a key lives or how it is protected.

_why: 🔴 THE PIN THAT CATCHES A KEY BEING SWAPPED, not one being absent. Until 2026-08-04 nothing
in this repository read the signature of a built artifact, and every .aab CI produced was
DEBUG-SIGNED while every configuration check stayed green — the config had been correct for
weeks and no workflow supplied the secrets, so the recorded debug fallback fired on every run.
tooling/ci/assert-artifact-signed.mjs now reads the real signer out of the bundle. This field
is what turns 'signed by SOME non-debug key' into 'signed by OUR key'.
WHY PINNING IS WORTH ITS BRITTLENESS. Play fixes the upload certificate at the FIRST upload
and refuses every later bundle signed by another key, so a secret quietly swapped for a
different-but-valid keystore — a copy-paste between repositories, a half-applied rotation, a
restore from the wrong backup — passes every other check and fails AT THE STORE. Against that,
the cost is one line edited during an upload-key reset, which is already a deliberate,
multi-step request to Google and never something that happens by accident.
IT IS NOT A SECRET. This is the SHA-256 of a PUBLIC certificate: the Play Console displays it,
App Links' assetlinks.json requires it in plaintext, and it is inside every artifact the key
signs. Publishing it here discloses nothing that shipping a signed app does not.
⚠️ OWNER-ASSERTED AND UNVERIFIED BY ANY MACHINE IN THIS REPOSITORY. The keystore lives in the
gitignored release-keystore/ and CI has never held it, so this value was transcribed from the
owner's `keytool -list -v` output on the date below and nothing here has confirmed it. That is
an acceptable state because the failure mode is loud and immediate: the first release-signed
build prints the fingerprint it actually found beside the one expected here, so a transcription
error costs one CI run and names its own fix.
uploadCertificate._aliasNote: Renamed from `subly` on 2026-08-04 by [ADR 030] — ONE SHARED UPLOAD KEY FOR THE WHOLE FACTORY, so a per-app alias was the wrong name. This field kept saying `subly` afterwards and NOTHING NOTICED, because `keytool -changealias` leaves the SHA-256 byte-identical (that identity is the proof it was a rename and not a regeneration) and no guard reads this field — assert-artifact-signed.mjs consumes only `.sha256`. A value with no reader drifts silently and its `asOf` date goes on looking fresh. The repo secret ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS is the authority.

_sourceCorrection: 🔴 THIS LINE USED TO RECOMMEND `Get-PfxCertificate <file> | Format-List Subject,Thumbprint`, AND

corrected rather than left as the thing the guard has to apologise for.
WHAT A SHA-256 THUMBPRINT IS, so any command can be checked against the definition rather than
trusted: the SHA-256 digest of the certificate's DER encoding. Hashing the DER-encoded public
certificate file therefore IS the thumbprint — which is why the file-hash commands below are
codeSigningCertificate.source: To be transcribed from the issued certificate on the day OWNER_QUEUE's code-signing purchase completes. channels.name: AppImage from dl.nikatru.com

signing.custody: does not exist — no store gatekeeper verifies this one, so the signature is only worth what our custody of it is worth.

_why: 🔴 THE PUBLIC HALF, PINNED — WHICH ON THIS ROW IS THE WHOLE VERIFICATION STORY. Every other
channel has a gatekeeper that checks a signature for somebody: Play pins the upload
certificate, the Microsoft Store re-signs, Canonical signs the snap, Apple's Gatekeeper
verifies at launch. `own-signing-key` means NOBODY DOES. `custody` above says so in prose;
this block is the mechanical consequence — the only thing that can ever tell a user (or a
later CI run) that an .AppImage came from us is comparing its detached signature to a public
key published somewhere they already trust, and this register is that somewhere.
THE PATTERN IS android-play's `uploadCertificate`, ONE ROW OVER, and its reasoning transfers
line for line: a key quietly swapped for a different-but-valid one — a half-applied rotation,
a restore from the wrong backup, a copy-paste between repositories — produces an artifact that
verifies perfectly against the WRONG identity. Pinning is what turns 'signed by some key' into
'signed by OUR key'. The same shape already exists in this tree for content packs: `k1` is
pinned in packages/core/lib/src/content/pack_verifier.dart rather than fetched.
IT IS NOT A SECRET, AND NOTHING HERE EVER WILL BE. This is the PUBLIC half of a keypair; the
seed's custody is `nonChannelSigningIdentities`-style private-SSoT work (compare
content-pack-k1, whose entry was REDACTED on 2026-07-31 precisely because a public register
must say THAT custody is recorded, never where a key lives).
⬜ SENTINEL-VALUED: no key has been generated (`restoreDrill.note`), so there is no public key
to record. The placeholder cannot be mistaken for one — an Ed25519 public key is 32 bytes and
44 base64 characters, and this is neither. assert-channel-register.mjs reads the sentinel: a
SERVED row still carrying it FAILS, a deferred row PRINTS ([pipeline C-6]), and a half-filled
block FAILS in either state.

rows each carry a passphrase alongside their key material because PKCS#12 is the container
their tools accept and it is encrypted by construction. A raw Ed25519 seed has no such

secret storage and the environment protection rules on the lane, which is what

_tellsWhy: EVERY STRING THAT ADVERTISES THIS CHANNEL, not just its id. `assert-channel-claims.mjs` scans
these tokens case-insensitively over RAW site text. The id alone was not enough, proven by
mutation 2026-07-31: a public surface reading "install the flatpak from your distro store"
passed clean, because `flatpak` is the package FORMAT and `flathub` is the channel id. A reader
cannot tell the difference and neither can a store reviewer. The guard REQUIRES this array —
non-empty and containing the id — so deleting or emptying it FAILS instead of silently
narrowing the scan to the id alone (hardened 2026-07-31 after a mutation proved the old
fallback made exactly that narrowing silent).
⚠️ `.deb` and `apt` are deliberately NOT here: [ADR 015] rejected them as OPTIONS, it did not
disqualify them as channels, and a token that broad would fire on any prose about Linux.
reason: Flathub's requirements page bans AI-generated or AI-assisted code, documentation or any other
content, and says such submissions can be rejected without review with repeat violations risking
a permanent ban. This repo's public git history carries Claude co-author trailers and cannot be
rewritten, so we cannot comply — and a publisher-wide ban is existential against L21's single
store identity. AMENDS lock L12 ('Linux = Flathub first').
⬜ OWNER_QUEUE A-5 still reads PENDING for this channel, and site copy still carries live Flathub
documents instruct a submission a LOCKED ADR forbids. [10]D-4's and [10]D-1's job, not R-5's.

_serviceEnvironmentsWhy: 🔴 A BACKEND WORKER IS NOT A RELEASE CHANNEL, and record-deployment.mjs used to insist it was.
Since [10]D-9 (commit 3a16272) that script resolved EVERY environment against `channels` and
hard-failed when none matched — so `deploy-workers.yml` went red on `subly-api` and `platform`
from 2026-08-02, five consecutive runs, AFTER both Workers had uploaded successfully.
The matcher was right and the register was the wrong authority. A `channels` row carries
`platforms`, `artifactFormats`, `signing.keyKind`, `minimumToolchain`, `lane` and
`storeMetadataDir`; a Worker has none of them. Worse, `channels` is the derived right-hand side
for assert-channel-register.mjs, assert-release-lane-generic.mjs, assert-store-identity.mjs and
assert-store-metadata.mjs, all of which quantify over {served rows} × {apps} — a fake `subly-api`
row would corrupt every one. And `platform` is not app-scoped at all: the only template that
could match it is a bare "{app}", whose head and tail are both empty, so it would swallow EVERY
environment string and destroy the matcher for real channels.
So these get their own list, exactly as `nonChannelSigningIdentities` does for the pack key.
`resolveEnvironment` falls through to here and returns `kind: 'service'`, which is not 'store',
so the listing-URL rule in record-deployment.mjs and the submission filter in readSubmissions
both continue to behave correctly. An environment that appears in NEITHER list is still refused —
that failing input is preserved, which is what keeps this a fix and not a weakening.
tooling/ci/test/deployment-record.test.mjs derives every `record-deployment.mjs <env>` call site
from the real workflows and asserts each one resolves against THIS file, so the next unclaimed
environment fails on the PR that adds it rather than on a production deploy, four times over.
